newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Wednesday were bid $67.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00 to $69.00, feedlot sources said.
"If $68.00 (bids) come, it will buy the world," one Kansas feedlot source said.
Sales last week started at $68.00, but slipped to $67.00 on Thursday.

Prices this week were expected to return to the $68.00 level amid a rebound in wholesale beef prices, which was tied to active buying by retailers for promotions following the Easter holiday on March 30, sources said.
Sales were expected to occur soon because packers reportedly were short of cattle and needed to replenish supply to meet the growing beef demand, several sources said.
Beef prices on Tuesday were quoted up $0.58 to $1.13 per cwt, with 170 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted up $1.13 at $103.39, a $1.60 jump since prices started climbing on Friday.
However, the firmer tone to the cash cattle market could fade if live cattle futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange trade sharply lower, cattle feeders said.
